title: The Letters
subtitle: The Zodiac ciphers · Northern California, 1969
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a late-1960s San Francisco newspaper office at night, wooden desks, manual typewriters, paper and envelopes, green-shaded lamps, cold blue-grey window light with fog outside, melancholy and uncanny, period 1969 detail, cinematic composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no legible writing, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Northern California, nineteen sixty-nine. Three newspapers received letters from a killer, each holding one third of a code.
beats.img: Three plain white envelopes lying on a cluttered late-1960s newspaper desk under a green-shaded lamp, a typewriter and an ashtray beside them, night, the addresses turned away and unreadable, no people.

beats.vo: He demanded they print it. Within about a week, a schoolteacher and his wife in Salinas had broken it.
beats.img: A kitchen table in a modest 1969 California home at night, sheets of graph paper covered in faint pencil grids and blurred illegible marks, a pencil and a cup of coffee, warm lamp light, no people.

beats.vo: Months later came a second code. Three hundred and forty symbols. It stayed unsolved for fifty-one years.
beats.img: A single greeting-card-sized sheet of paper pinned to a corkboard in a dim newspaper office, covered in tiny blurred illegible hand-drawn marks, shallow focus, cold window light, dust in the air, no people.

beats.vo: In twenty twenty, three amateur codebreakers finally cracked it. It did not contain his name.
beats.img: An old yellowed sheet of paper with blurred illegible marks lying beside a modern laptop glowing in a dark room at night, the screen showing only soft abstract light, quiet and still, no people.

beats.vo: Two shorter codes have never been confirmed solved. And the writer has never been officially identified.
beats.img: An empty late-1960s newspaper office at night, rows of silent typewriters on wooden desks, a single lamp left on, fog pressing against tall dark windows, cold and unresolved, no people.

facts.claim: On July 31, 1969 three nearly identical letters went to the San Francisco Chronicle, San Francisco Examiner and Vallejo Times-Herald, each enclosing one third of a 408-symbol cipher, with a demand that it be printed
The 408 cipher was broken within about a week (Aug 1969) by Donald Harden, a Salinas schoolteacher, and his wife Bettye
The 340-symbol cipher was mailed to the Chronicle on November 8, 1969 and went unsolved for 51 years
Z340 was decrypted in December 2020 by private citizens David Oranchak, Sam Blake and Jarl Van Eycke; FBI acknowledged it; the message does not name the killer
The two shorter ciphers (Z13, April 1970; Z32, June 1970) have no confirmed solution
The killer has never been identified; the case remains open (SFPD reopened 2006; FBI called it ongoing in 2020); 2025-26 independent claims unconfirmed by any agency
